title: Abaye, an Early Second-Generation Amora in the Land of Israel
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Jerusalem Talmud] Rosh Hashanah, chapter 1, halakhah 5: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish raised a question — Abaye objected, and he (Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish) did not accept it from him. In Megillah, end of chapter 2, the statement is cited, and there he is called Rabbi Abaye. And in Sukkah, chapter 2, halakhah 8: Rabbi Chuna in the name of Rav Avaya. And in Terumot, chapter 5, halakhah 4: Rabbi Yonah in the name of Rabbi Abaye. And in the R”Sh the reading is: Rabbi Yirmiyah in the name of Rabbi Immi.

notes.text: This notice explicitly concerns an early Amora in the Land of Israel. Abaye, Avaya and Immi remain the recorded alternatives, distinct from the better-known Babylonian sage. The final commentator siglum is kept as R”Sh.

The named Rosh Hashanah parallel was found in the consulted Jerusalem Talmud chapter 1, halakhah 8, rather than the supplied 1:5. The supplied locator remains Hyman’s; the passage does not establish identity with the Babylonian Abaye.
